top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct mechanism from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion prizes: it cancels light shift, Doppler and recoil effects together while interrogating many atoms in parallel, has been reproduced independently near 1e-18, and enables tests of relativity, varying constants and dark matter. The two-name allocation (Katori for the scheme and first realisation, Ye for the accuracy and many-body frontier) is the least contested on the shortlist and defensible as written, and the citation is scoped to the lattice scheme rather than precision in general. No award is the only alternative and would be a worse outcome than this mature, confirmed achievement.
